title: MathEstimatorProof
description: Proof object required to STRONG-CLEAR a math-estimator-sensitive coverage item (estimator/guard/formula/precision logic). A clear of such an item is INVALID on NatSpec/code consistency alone ('code matches comments', 'formula appears consistent', 'guard clamps the output', 'same pattern as sibling rule'). The clear must independently re-derive the intended formula/invariant and check edge cases. See documentation/math_estimator_proof_policy.md. Reference schema only (no runtime loader); validate_math_estimator_clears.py enforces these fields in Python.

math_domain.description: The math surface this estimator/guard belongs to.

intended_formula.description: The formula/invariant the code is SUPPOSED to implement, stated from the whitepaper / model / spec — not paraphrased from the code's own comments.

implemented_formula.description: The formula the code ACTUALLY computes, read off the implementation (operations, order, scaling).

formula_source.description: Where the intended_formula came from. If this is ONLY {NatSpec, code}, the clear is natspec_only and INVALID unless 'limitations' explains why an external source was unavailable AND an independent re-derivation was still performed.

independent_rederivation.description: The reviewer's own step-by-step re-derivation comparing intended vs implemented (e.g. expand the recurrence, check the (1-lambda) placement, the outer-product scaling, the sign). MUST be non-empty for a valid clear.

input_domain.description: Valid ranges/units of the inputs (e.g. lambda in (0,1), prices 18dp, n assets).

scaling_precision.description: Fixed-point scaling and precision handling (1e9 pack / 1e18 / 1e36, mul-before-div).

rounding_behavior.description: Rounding direction and where truncation occurs; whether it favors the protocol.

signedness_assumptions.description: Signed vs unsigned handling; can intermediate values go negative; sign-flip risks.

bounds_and_guards.description: Bounds/guard rails relied on AND independently confirmed (not merely cited).

edge_cases_checked.description: Concrete edge cases re-derived (zero/extreme inputs, n=1, division by ~0, overflow threshold, odd/even token counts). MUST be non-empty.

invariant_preserved.description: The protocol invariant that holds after the computation (e.g. weights sum to 1, variance >= 0).

evidence_span.description: file:line span(s) anchoring the implemented_formula. MUST be non-empty.

limitations.description: What the re-derivation could NOT confirm; required justification when formula_source is NatSpec/code-only.

formula_diff.description: Explicit line-by-line difference between intended_formula and implemented_formula (operations, order, scaling, constants). State 'no divergence' ONLY if it was adversarially confirmed against an external/economic expectation, not merely because the code matches itself.

assumptions.description: Assumptions the re-derivation relies on (input ranges, caller trust, upstream guarantees). Each must be independently justified, not assumed from the code.

monotonicity_and_economic_direction.description: Expected monotonic/economic direction of the output and how it must move with the relevant economic variable(s) (fee/stake/difficulty/price/reward/weight/time/supply/…), compared against what the code actually does. MUST name at least one economic variable.

attacker_favorable_search.description: Adversarial parameter search: extreme/boundary/attacker-favorable inputs tried (max/min, 2**k boundaries, zero, overflow threshold) and the divergence/overflow/precision-loss/monotonicity-inversion found or ruled out. Required when the formula uses shift/scaling (<<, >>, **, 1e..).

economic_impact_if_wrong.description: Concrete protocol/user/attacker consequence if the formula is wrong (over/under-charged fee, mispriced reward, drained pool, DoS) — the 'so what' that makes a divergence a finding.
